purpose: Defects M00 confirmed and reproduced, each with a test that runs on every build. An open defect is characterised by a test asserting the CURRENT, broken behaviour; a fixed defect keeps the same test asserting the fix, so the defect cannot quietly come back. Fixing one without updating this file makes the corresponding test fail, which is the point: the fix has to be a deliberate act, not a drift nobody notices.
note: Read the entry's status and owner fields before changing a test. A failing test here means one of three things, and the failure message says which: the phase named in owner has landed and this registry needs updating, a fixed defect has regressed, or an untouched defect changed behaviour.
statusVocabulary: open - the defect is present; its test asserts the broken behaviour and fails when the defect is fixed
fixed - the defect is gone; its test asserts the correct behaviour and fails if the defect returns
partially fixed - the specified half is fixed and the rest is owned by another phase; the entry says which half

defects.title: FailureCode.RESOLVER_INIT_FAILED is declared, translated for the user, and unreachable
defects.fixedIn: the resolver-init branch of FailureCode.classify, matching the engine's own name in the stage hint or the throwable message
defects.current_behaviour: FailureCode.classify() returns CLASS_NOT_FOUND, MEMBER_NOT_FOUND, ACCESS_DENIED, TIMEOUT, RESOLVER_AMBIGUOUS or UNEXPECTED. It has no branch returning RESOLVER_INIT_FAILED, and no production code constructs a report with that code.
defects.symptom: The one failure mode the code was written for - the module could not initialise DexKit - is never reported. UserExplanation has a sentence for it that can never be shown.
defects.root_cause: FeatureLoader.start() runs before Instrumentation.callApplicationOnCreate, so FailureReportStore has no Application to attach to. The failure is logged to the Xposed log and start() returns with zero hooks installed.
defects.fixedWording: The test now asserts the fix from both sides: the function must contain a path that returns RESOLVER_INIT_FAILED, and one concrete DexKit-style failure must classify as it, while a failure that names neither the engine nor the stage still reports UNEXPECTED rather than being attributed to the engine.

defects.title: DexKit initialisation failure installs zero hooks and reports nothing
defects.fixedHalf: The failure is no longer silent. Health exists before the engine is asked to initialise, the stage is opened, and the failure is recorded against the DEXKIT subsystem with RuntimeFailureCode.DEXKIT_INIT_FAILED instead of only being logged. The ordering is asserted, not just the presence: the record has to exist before the step that can fail.
defects.remainingHalf: The early return is deliberately unchanged, so this failure still stops the bootstrap and installs nothing. What should happen instead of returning - which stages are safe to continue with - is #322 M03's decision, and it needs the record to exist first. The same is true of the persistence: the record is in-process because nothing has a usable data directory this early, and the manager-visible surface arrives with the stage runner.
defects.current_behaviour: Unobfuscator.initWithPath catches every Exception and returns a bare false. FeatureLoader.start() logs "Can't init dexkit" and returns before installing any hook.
defects.symptom: WhatsApp starts with no WA X behaviour at all, nothing on any surface the user can read, and the WA X app still shows "Module enabled" with a version number because the self-hook fired in a different process.
defects.root_cause: Same as M00-DEF-01: no reporting channel exists before Application.onCreate.
defects.fixedWording: The test asserts both halves: the failure is recorded with DEXKIT_INIT_FAILED, and the early return is still there so that removing it without a decision reads as a failure naming M03 rather than as a silent behaviour change.

defects.title: The status banner is the module's opinion of itself, not the runtime's state
defects.current_behaviour: isXposedEnabled() is System.currentTimeMillis() == 0L, which is unconditionally false unhooked. Its only true path is a self-hook returning a constant, installed only when LSPosed loads WA X into its own process. HomeFragment.checkStateWpp() branches on it alone.
defects.symptom: The banner means "LSPosed is running and has WA X in its own scope". It cannot be affected by WhatsApp's scope, the target process, injection, preferences, DexKit, resolvers or any feature.
defects.root_cause: Self-hook as an activation signal is circular: the module reports itself healthy because it is running.

defects.title: modulePath is passed to XModuleResources.createInstance without a null guard
defects.current_behaviour: modulePath is String? and assigned only in initZygote. createInstance's first parameter is a Java platform type, so Kotlin accepts passing null when initZygote has not run.
defects.symptom: Resource injection is handed a null module path. The failure mode is not asserted here because it depends on LSPosed callback ordering that cannot be reproduced off-device.
defects.root_cause: A nullable field is consumed by a platform-typed Java call with no guard.

defects.title: Resource injection swallows every exception, so it fails silently
defects.current_behaviour: The loop that walks R.array, R.string and R.drawable and rewrites their static int fields is wrapped in catch (_: Exception) {} with an empty body.
defects.symptom: A failed injection means WA X's resources silently do not apply while the banner reads "enabled".
defects.root_cause: An empty catch turns a real failure into a missing feature. Counted under silent_catch in the M00.06 inventory.
